title: Climb the Next Step
subject: English
source: Written for english/y7 lesson 56 (Speech 'Climb the Next Step' (teacher-written model speech to a Year 7 assembly, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 56. A teacher-written model speech to a Year 7 assembly. Read it aloud, annotate the devices, then compare it with the poem.

passage.title: Climb the Next Step
paras: Assalamu alaikum, everyone. Thank you for letting me speak to you this morning.

When I was your age, I failed my first reading test. Not once: twice. I remember the red pen and the long walk home. My grandmother did not tell me I was clever. She said, 'Tomorrow, read one page more than today.' So I did. One page became ten; ten became a book; a book became a love of reading that has never left me. You will fall. You will be tired. You will want to stop. Do not stop. Climb the next step.

Some of you are finding Year 7 hard. The work is new, the corridors are long and the homework never seems to end. I know, because I have been there. But every person you admire in this school, every teacher, every Year 11 who walks so confidently down the corridor, was once exactly where you are now.

So here is my challenge. This week, do one thing more than last week. Read one page more. Ask one question more. Try one problem more. It will not feel like much. But steps add up, and one day you will look back and see how high you have climbed. Do not stop. Climb the next step.

questions.q: Who is the audience and what is the purpose?
questions.a: Year 7 pupils in an assembly; to inspire them to keep going when learning is hard.

questions.q: Find the image the speech shares with Mother to Son
Core: in the portal response box, write a PEEDL paragraph: 'Compare how the speech and the poem encourage perseverance.' Starter: 'Both texts encourage perseverance by...'
questions.a: A PEEDL paragraph: both use climbing and personal experience; the speech uses anecdote and the rule of three, the poem an extended metaphor and a mother's voice.

questions.q: Extend: write a fourth line for the rule of three that keeps the pattern
Stretch: which text inspires you more, and why?
questions.a: A reasoned choice referring to methods (anecdote, metaphor, voice).

questions.q: Why does the speaker begin with a story about failing?
options: to show the audience that struggle is normal and can be overcome
questions.a: B) to show the audience that struggle is normal and can be overcome. An anecdote of failure builds trust and hope.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: how do speakers inspire people?
questions.a: For example: by sharing their own struggle and ending with a clear call to action.
